messages.text:
PhysVal-05 assessed source **`c2453e91255c023f724028f2eb5f1b0f365106c3`** and the native outputs bound by retained inventory SHA-256 **`b8709852ba103e36a68e21f8de0df61b4b02ab30b2c3ebbddf1402259f4d18bf`**. All twelve native report/full-array hash bindings passed. No files changed.

For **100 GeV, |η| < 1**, all four cases contain the same **5,036 finite, matched fits with valid covariance**. Measurement counts agree, so the apparent improvement is not survivor bias.

| Pitch | z₀ core width [µm] | z₀ SD [µm] | z₀ pull SD | Median predicted σz₀ [µm] |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.5 mm | 4.021 | 5.214 | 0.543 | 8.713 |
| 1 mm | 3.556 | 5.105 | 0.492 | 9.145 |
| 1.5 mm | 3.295 | 5.029 | 0.474 | 9.249 |
| 2 mm | 3.093 | 4.898 | 0.458 | 9.281 |

The 2 mm z₀ core-width ratio is **0.769 ± 0.014**, while the uncut SD ratio is approximately **0.939**. The theta result behaves similarly. Biases remain small; pT, d₀ and phi remain nearly unchanged. The strongest effect occurs around **|η| = 0.25–0.75**, with approximate positive/negative symmetry.

No coordinate-swap or segmentation-isolation error was found: complete digitization configurations become identical after restoring only the 12,384 strixel local-v grids.

The response is visibly uncalibrated. In the existing small measurement-writing pilot, central pixel local-v normalized residual SD is **0.447**, versus **1.011** for baseline strixels. Coarser strixel hit RMS worsens from **118 to 538 µm**, while pixel measurements stay identical. This supports an interpretation involving covariance weighting and geometric clustering, but does not establish the complete high-pT mechanism.

A separate **100 GeV Gaussian p/√12 control**, preferably 5,000 paired events per pitch, would materially clarify the tradeoff. Report the observed geometric result conditionally; it does **not** establish that coarser sensors physically improve tracking. Calibrated incidence/charge-sharing/noise response remains necessary for selecting a baseline.
